text: Continuous Integration, or CI, is a software development practice where developers regularly merge their code changes into a shared repository. Instead of waiting until the end of a project, changes are integrated multiple times a day. The core of CI is the pipeline, which is an automated process that runs every time new code is added. This pipeline includes automated builds, which compile the code, and running tests to check if everything works correctly. The main advantage is catching issues early, before they become bigger problems. If a test fails, the team is alerted immediately, allowing them to fix the error quickly. This leads to more reliable software and a smoother, more collaborative workflow for the whole team.
